en.title: j in jam (/dʒ/)
en.summary: This item illustrates the letter j representing the sound /dʒ/ as in the word jam.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs: You call this group /dʒe/ or /dʒi/. Its primary pronunciation is the sound /d͡ʒ/, that is a voiced jam sound, heard in (gem) /ˈd͡ʒem/, meaning frost, severe cold. It produces two distinct sounds.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Touch the roof of your mouth with your tongue tip. Push air through firmly while your vocal cords vibrate, and release. For the second sound, make this same release while flattening your tongue against the roof. Feel your neck buzz with your fingers.

sections.title: Reading the letters
paragraphs: Before the vowels e or i, read the sound /d͡ʒ/, that is a full voiced jam sound. You hear this sound in (ger) /d͡ʒer/. At the end of a word after this group, make the sound /d͡ʒʲ/, that is a softened voiced sound. This occurs in (dragi) /drad͡ʒʲ/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not turn this letter group into the hard sound in get. Speak it gently as in judge. At the end of a word, do not add a full vowel like English energy. Cut the airflow instantly.
